transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alice Reed (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood SDR); Priya Nair (CTO), Damien Cole (Security Lead), Sofia Ruiz (Head of ML), Ethan Morris (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on security posture for Lark's platform, lots of questions on SSO, KMS, and audit logs. Agreement to share SOC2, SAML integration docs, and schedule a follow-up technical deep dive.

[00:00] Alice Reed: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do quick intros, i'm alice reeed with redwood, thats alice reed, sorry, and marcus is our se, jordan's here to take notes
[00:12] Priya Nair: hi, priya here, CTO at lark analytics, we've been evaluating a few inference providers and we need to validate security posture before a pilot
[00:20] Damien Cole: hey all, damien, security lead. main concerns are SOC2/ISO, SSO via SAML, audit logs, and how you manage keys - K M S - and data retention windows
[00:30] Marcus Li: thanks, yeah so quick overview: on hosted we maintain SOC2 Type II, iso alignment, encryption at rest with customer-unique keys supported via KMS integrations. Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and better network isolation, and Private is full VPC-onprem options if you need complete control
[01:05] Sofia Ruiz: can you clarify the difference between hosted with customer-managed KMS vs Private? like who has access to keys?
[01:15] Marcus Li: sure - for hosted we offer a customer-managed KMS option where the customer supplies keys via a cloud KMS and we use them for encryption at rest; Redwood operators do not have access to plaintext keys, and there are HSM-backed options. For Private, the keys remain entirely under customer control inside their VPC or on-prem HSMs
[01:45] Ethan Morris: and network? we have strict egress rules, need to ensure traffic doesn't route outside our VPC for private deployments
[01:53] Marcus Li: Private deployments run inside your VPC or on-prem, so all inference traffic stays within your network; Dedicated has peered networking and private endpoints, hosted uses TLS over the public internet but we can offer customer-specific private endpoints for enterprise accounts
[02:20] Damien Cole: regarding compliance, do you provide SOC2 report and ISO certs? we need to share with procurement
[02:28] Alice Reed: yes we can share SOC2 Type II report, and a ISO/IEC 27001 summary; i'll attach both. there's also our security whitepaper and third party pen test summary
[02:40] Priya Nair: what's your data retention policy for logs and for input data? we cannot keep PII beyond 90 days in our environment
[02:50] Marcus Li: by default hosted keeps logs for 30 days, you can configure retention for longer; input data is not stored unless you opt-in for logging for debugging; for Dedicated and Private you control retention policies and can set retention to meet 90-day requirement or shorter
[03:15] Damien Cole: audit logs - what do you provide for audit trail? immutable logs? can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[03:24] Marcus Li: we provide detailed audit logs with user, token, model used, timestamp, and request metadata. Logs are immutable write-once in our log store; for enterprise customers we stream logs to customer SIEM or to their S3 bucket, or push to a syslog endpoint
[03:45] Priya Nair: SSO question - we use Okta and ADFS for different teams, we require SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning ideally
[03:55] Marcus Li: we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. i will share the SAML metadata and the required attributes (email, name, groups, role). sometimes auto-transcription says SAMEL (laugh) but it's SAML
[04:18] Damien Cole: RBAC - we need least-privilege roles and service account separation for pipelines vs devs
[04:25] Marcus Li: Redwood supports org-level RBAC, role templates (admin, developer, viewer) and service principals for machine-to-machine with scoped permissions. You can create custom roles and apply attribute-based restrictions to routes and models
[04:40] Sofia Ruiz: do you have separation of duties between support and ops? we don't want support to be able to decrypt user data
[04:48] Alice Reed: yes we follow least privilege – support cannot access customer data or keys; access to KMS is gated by IAM and audit logging. for hosted we have strict internal controls and for Dedicated/Private you get even stronger isolation
[05:05] Priya Nair: encryption in transit? how is that handled between client and API and between services internally
[05:12] Marcus Li: TLS 1.2/1.3 for client->api; internal service-to-service is mTLS in Dedicated/Private and encrypted links with perfect forward secrecy in hosted. We can provide cipher suites and cert rotation policy docs
[05:30] Ethan Morris: for our SOC we need evidence of certificate rotation and key management policies
[05:36] Marcus Li: we can provide KMS rotation policies, key lifecycle docs, and logs of rotation events as part of compliance package
[05:50] Damien Cole: incident response - what's your process and SLA for notifying customers of breaches or incidents?
[05:58] Alice Reed: our incident response policy includes 72-hour notification for incidents that affect customer data, we have runbooks, and you get a dedicated account security contact for enterprise deals
[06:12] Priya Nair: any certifications for physical security where your data centers are?
[06:18] Marcus Li: we rely on cloud providers with SOC 2/ISO compliant facilities and can provide the provider attestations; for Private on-prem obviously that goes to you
[06:30] Sofia Ruiz: curious about model artifacts – do you ever cache model outputs and could that be considered persistent PII?
[06:38] Marcus Li: we do prefix/KV caching to speed up generation; hosted caching is configurable and you can disable caching of any prompt/response that contains sensitive data. Default configs avoid persisting PII but customers can opt-in to more extensive caching for performance during PoC
[06:58] Damien Cole: can you redact or tokenise inputs server-side? we prefer client-side tokenisation but want options
[07:06] Marcus Li: generally we recommend client-side tokenisation, but we offer middleware options and can integrate with your pipeline to redact before it reaches Redwood; this is easier on Dedicated/Private where you control the runtime
[07:30] Alice Reed: what about legal - do you do a DPA and can we get data processing terms with specific retention clauses?
[07:38] Priya Nair: procurement will need that before we sign a PO
[07:42] Alice Reed: yes we have a standard DPA and can negotiate retention terms for enterprise contracts; i'll loop in our legal enablement if you want specifics
[07:54] Ethan Morris: performance - unrelated but important: if we run a PoC on Dedicated, can we test latency and have reproducible benchmarks?
[08:02] Marcus Li: absolutely, for Dedicated we can provision a test cluster and run benchmarks; we'll also share our benchmarking harness and grain-level metrics (p50/p95/p99)
[08:18] Damien Cole: back to SSO - do you support enforced 2FA and device trust?
[08:24] Marcus Li: yes, we support enforcing 2FA via SAML IdP and device-based constraints if your IdP provides them; we also support SCIM for provisioning/ disabling accounts
[08:38] Priya Nair: audit log retention length - we might need 12 months of logs for compliance
[08:45] Marcus Li: for enterprise you can set retention to 12+ months; we also support archiving to your S3 for long term retention and e-discovery exports
[08:58] Sofia Ruiz: any rate limits that leak user identifiers into logs? our policy forbids leaking user email in telemetry
[09:06] Marcus Li: logs redact PII by default but you can opt into more verbose logs for debugging; redaction rules are configurable and we can sign an agreement about not storing email addresses in telemetry unless you opt-in
[09:24] Damien Cole: how are service accounts scoped for apps vs humans? we need different tokens with restricted scopes
[09:30] Marcus Li: service principals have scoped grants; tokens can be short-lived and tied to specific routes/models; we support fine-grained scopes for embed vs generate vs admin APIs
[09:46] Alice Reed: quick check — does your legal/compliance team require on-prem deployment, or would dedicated with peering and customer-managed KMS be sufficient?
[09:55] Priya Nair: we'd prefer not to go fully on-prem if we can avoid it, Dedicated with peering + customer KMS might work, procurement will still ask for DPA and SOC2 certs
[10:10] Damien Cole: curious about multi-tenant isolation in hosted - what guarantees exist if another tenant is noisy or compromised
[10:20] Marcus Li: multi-tenant isolation is at process and container boundaries, we use kernel hardening and cgroups and monitor noisy neighbours; fallback is to move you to Dedicated where you get reserved GPUs and tenancy isolation
[10:40] Ethan Morris: encryption key rotation frequency? we have a policy of rotating keys every 90 days
[10:45] Marcus Li: we can align with that, KMS supports automated rotation or manual; for hosted with customer KMS you control rotation cadence
[11:05] Priya Nair: what certifications do you have for personnel background checks? we need vendor attestations
[11:12] Alice Reed: we can provide our HR controls summary and background check policies for staff with access to infra, and SOC2 covers some of that scope
[11:30] Damien Cole: can we run a security audit or pentest against a Dedicated instance? we often require a pentest during procurement
[11:36] Marcus Li: yes, we allow pentests on dedicated/private and we have a coordinated disclosure and testing window; we can provide pentest scopes and rules of engagement
[11:52] Priya Nair: any support for data residency? we have EU customers and need EU-only processing for certain datasets
[11:58] Marcus Li: we have regional deployment options and can restrict processing to Europe regions; for full EU-only guarantees Private or Dedicated in a European cloud region is the best path
[12:20] Alice Reed: ok let's put concrete next steps, i'll send SOC2 + ISO + DPA, marcus will send SAML metadata and the SE checklist, and we'll propose a date for the technical deep dive next week
[12:35] Priya Nair: works for us, thanks everyone
[12:40] Damien Cole: thanks, appreciate the thoroughness

Action items recap:
- Alice to send SOC2 Type II and ISO summary (6/16)
- Marcus to send SAML metadata, SCIM attributes, and SE security checklist (6/18)
- Priya to share architecture diagram and residency requirements (6/19)

Notes: occasional transcription errors (SAMEL for SAML, K M S spelled out), some speaker labels merged early in the call due to echo.
